10 Beachfront Hotels with Great Vibes
Koh Samet, Rayong

heroSub: 10 hand-picked beachfront hotels and resorts on Koh Samet that we've reviewed in depth — clear-water Ao Prao on the west side, lively Sai Kaew Beach in the middle of the island, quiet bays at the island's tip, plus bungalows and cottages set in seaside gardens. Prices start at about ฿1,500–4,500/night.
introH2: 🏖️ What kinds of Koh Samet beach hotels are there, and which beach suits your trip?
introHtml: Koh Samet is smaller than many people expect, but each beach has a completely different feel — and that's exactly why choosing where to stay here takes more thought than just comparing prices. Sai Kaew Beach in the middle of the island is the liveliest stretch: step out of your room and you're among restaurants, live music, and fire shows after dark — great for anyone who likes a bit of buzz. Ao Prao on the west side is a quiet, clear-water beach where you can snorkel over coral right off the sand and watch a lovely sunset, but you have to take a boat into the bay. Meanwhile Ao Phai, Ao Cho, Lung Dam Beach, and Ao Noina are quiet beaches that suit serious relaxation and families with young kids. A lot of people book by the pretty photos online and end up on a beach that's either too lively or too quiet for what they actually wanted. This article rounds up 10 beachfront hotels and resorts on Koh Samet that we've reviewed in depth, covering all the main beaches — every one drawn from reading real guest reviews, with honest pros and cons, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Koh Samet sits within Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park in Rayong. From Bangkok it's a 3–3.5 hour drive to Ban Phe pier, then a 30–40 min passenger-ferry crossing or a 15 min speedboat ride over to the island. There are no private cars on the island — you mostly get around by shared songthaew or on foot, and there's a national park entry fee at the pier. The beaches in this article: Sai Kaew Beach, near the Na Dan pier, walkable to everything and the liveliest. Ao Phai and Lung Dam Beach, next to Sai Kaew but quieter, within walking distance. Ao Prao on the west side, reached by boat or by crossing the island, quiet with clear water. Ao Cho and Ao Noina, quiet and private beaches that suit serious relaxation.

entries.storyHtml: If there's one stay on Koh Samet that many reviews single out as the most luxurious of the 10 in this article, it's Le Vimarn Cottages & Spa, a small 5-star resort in the Samed Resorts group tucked away on Ao Prao on the island's west side — and the highest score in this set at 9.3. What makes people fall for it is Ao Prao itself: a private beach that's quiet with very clear water. Honest takes from real reviews say the same thing — walk straight into the sea off the beach and you can snorkel over coral and fish, a world apart from the lively Sai Kaew Beach. All 31 cottages and villas are set climbing up the hillside, and many have soaking tubs on the terrace looking straight out over Ao Prao; the woodwork and design blend into the slope in a way reviewers call carefully done. The Premier Ocean Hillside rooms are the ones guests praise most for their sea views. Service is another point that draws steady compliments — it's a small resort where staff are friendly, remember guests' names, and look after you in a personal way, which suits couples and honeymoon trips after some peace and quiet. Honest notes from the reviews: getting there means taking the resort's speedboat into Ao Prao, so allow extra time; the pool is fairly small and shallow and some reviews flag its cleanliness; drink prices and equipment rental run high; the bay is so quiet there are almost no restaurants outside the resort; and at times plastic litter drifts onto the beach even though the resort clears it daily. The bottom line: this isn't the cheapest option, but it's the best value for the experience if you want a private beach, clear water, and the quiet of a small resort on Koh Samet.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want full sea views, go for the Premier Ocean Hillside rooms, the ones reviews praise most for the view. Check the resort's speedboat schedule into Ao Prao ahead of time, and bring your own snorkel gear to save on rental fees on the island.

entries.storyHtml: If you love Ao Prao but aren't ready to pay luxury-resort rates, Ao Prao Resort is the answer that honest takes from real reviews call the best-value starting point on the same beach — a 4-star boutique resort in the Samed Resorts group, scoring 9.0 from 190 reviews, sitting right next to Le Vimarn on Ao Prao on the island's west side. The main draw is the same as its top-tier neighbour: Ao Prao, quiet with clear water. Many guests describe snorkelling over coral off the beach, and the resort also runs free daily coral-snorkelling activities for guests. All 63 rooms are set along the hillside, many with private balconies looking out over Ao Prao, and there are rooms freshly renovated in 2024 that reviews say are noticeably larger and cooler. Prices start at ฿3,500, lighter than the luxury resort on the same bay, which makes it the choice many people land on when they want the Ao Prao atmosphere on a more reachable budget. It's one of the 10 stays in this article that leans toward value over luxury. Honest notes from the reviews: getting there means the same resort speedboat into Ao Prao; rooms that haven't been renovated yet have dated facilities and bathrooms starting to show wear; staff professionalism isn't consistent in places; the breakfast menu could use more variety; and the bay is so quiet there are almost no restaurants outside the resort. The bottom line: it suits anyone who wants the private, clear-water beach of Ao Prao at a lighter price — and it's worth asking for a room on the 2024-renovated side first.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: When booking, ask clearly whether the room is on the freshly renovated 2024 side, since the condition differs quite a bit. And ask about the times for the resort's free coral-snorkelling activity so you can plan to be there on schedule.

entries.addr: 8/1 Moo 4, Sai Kaew Beach, Phe Sub-district, Mueang Rayong
entries.storyHtml: Where the first two stays sell the quiet of Ao Prao, Sai Kaew Beach Resort sells the opposite — the buzz and convenience of being right on Sai Kaew Beach. It's a 4-star resort in the Samed Resorts group, scoring 9.0 from 581 reviews, the most reviews among the top three stays in this article. The standout point that honest takes from real reviews agree on is the location: it's in the middle of Sai Kaew Beach, the island's longest and liveliest stretch, where you step out of your room and reach the sea and several restaurants — no boat ride into a hidden bay like on the Ao Prao side. The resort has three separate outdoor pools plus a kids' pool, a beachside massage spa, and a gym. After dark there's live music and a fire show on the beach, a fun, lively atmosphere a quiet beach can't offer. Rooms are done in a seaside blue-and-white palette, many with balconies, and the 2024-renovated rooms are described in reviews as fresh and clean. It's one of the 10 stays in this article that suits families and anyone who wants the convenience of walking to everything. Honest notes from the reviews: Sai Kaew is the busiest beach on the island, so it isn't for anyone after quiet; older-zone rooms have poor soundproofing and rooms near the stage may hear the night music; service slows down when it's busy; food and drink prices at the resort run high; and you'll find the odd insect in the room, as is the way with beachfront stays on the island. The bottom line: it suits anyone who wants a resort within walking distance of the sea, restaurants, and entertainment on a reachable budget — and you should ask for a renovated room away from the stage.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a light sleeper, ask for a room far from the music stage and on the 2024-renovated side — it'll be quieter and fresher. If you're travelling as a family, look at the Family Pool Residence rooms near the pool.

cons: Sai Kaew Beach is busy; not for anyone after quiet

entries.type: Beachfront Resort 3-Star · Beachfront on Ao Phai
entries.name: Samed Villa Resort

tags: 🌳 Leafy tropical garden by the beach

entries.addr: 89 Moo 4, Ao Phai Beach, Phe Sub-district, Mueang Rayong
entries.storyHtml: Samed Villa Resort is the resort that honest takes from real reviews call the sweet spot between buzz and quiet — set at the southern end of Ao Phai, scoring 9.2 from 358 reviews, among the highest scores in this article's lighter price bracket. What people like is the leafy tropical-garden setting: rooms and villas are spread through a garden among coconut palms, with flowers, fountains, and stone-paved paths that feel private and at one with nature. The beach out front has white sand and clear water, good for snorkelling and for letting kids play in the shallows — and crucially, it's about a 10–15 min walk to Sai Kaew Beach, so you can head out for dinner and the lights and come back to sleep in a calm spot. The thing reviews mention most, and praise almost unanimously, is the breakfast: generous and tasty, with plenty of Thai, Asian, and Western options, eaten beachside in a lovely setting. Rooms are done in a contemporary Thai style, some with dark-stone, spa-like bathrooms. It's one of the 10 stays in this article that earns a high score on a budget that isn't expensive. Honest notes from the reviews: there's no pool here; some nights you can hear music from a nearby bar until around 2:30 a.m.; the beds are too firm for some, and there are mosquitoes in the garden in the evening; the beach out front is fairly short and the canvas loungers fill up fast on busy days; Wi-Fi weakens in some rooms deep in the garden; and it's a building that's been in use a long time, so it shows its age in the details. The bottom line: it suits anyone who wants to stay by the beach in a leafy garden setting, close to the buzz but still sleeping well, and who doesn't mind there being no pool.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose a Deluxe Sea View room if you want a sea view from the balcony, and avoid rooms deep in the garden if you're worried about Wi-Fi signal. Bring your own mosquito repellent for evenings in the garden.

entries.addr: 1/8 Moo 4, Ao Noina, Phe Sub-district, Mueang Rayong
entries.storyHtml: Mooban Talay Resort is the stay that honest takes from real reviews call the best fit for couples and anyone who wants to escape the bustle for a quiet rest by the sea — set on Ao Noina at the island's north-west tip, a bungalow resort of about 22 units, scoring 8.0 from as many as 716 reviews, the most reviews among this article's quiet beaches. What makes people choose it is the quiet: at the island's tip there's almost no traffic and no night music, and the beach out front has so few people it's nearly private. The bungalows are raised on stilts in the garden, and many open straight onto the beach; because it faces north-west it looks right out at the sunset over the sea, a spot reviews often praise for the evening view. There's a free shuttle boat between Nuanthip pier and the resort's private pier twice a day, handy if you arrive on schedule. There's a pool with a bar, which reviews say is safer than the sea when there are sea urchins among the rocks. It's one of the 10 stays in this article that leans hardest into privacy and nature. Honest notes from the reviews: it's at the island's tip, which is harder to reach; there are few restaurants and little entertainment outside the resort; you need to plan the shuttle-boat times well, and if you miss them you'll pay for a vehicle across the island; details in the rooms and around the pool are starting to show their age; some stretches of the bay have sea urchins among the rocks to watch for when swimming; and breakfast is fairly basic, with some packages not including it in the room rate. The bottom line: it's the best fit for couples and anyone set on a quiet rest at the island's tip, who doesn't mind the travel being more involved than the main beaches.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Check the free shuttle-boat times from Nuanthip pier carefully and book to match them — it saves the cost of a vehicle across the island. If you want the sunset view, ask for a beachfront bungalow, and bring shoes for walking around the sea urchins among the rocks.

entries.type: Beachfront Resort 3-Star · Beachfront on Ao Cho
entries.name: Ao Cho Grandview Hideaway Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Cho · quiet private beach · shallow clear water
entries.addr: 44 Moo 4, Ao Cho Beach, Phe Sub-district, Mueang Rayong
entries.storyHtml: Ao Cho Grandview Hideaway Resort is the resort that honest takes from real reviews call the best fit for families with young kids and anyone who wants a quiet, peaceful Koh Samet — set on Ao Cho, a resort of about 35 rooms, scoring 8.1 from more than 2,990 reviews, the most reviews of all 10 stays in this article. The standout point guests agree on is that the resort takes up nearly the whole of Ao Cho, with fine white sand and water so shallow and clear you can see the bottom — fine for letting young kids into the water with peace of mind — and a beach quiet enough to feel like your own. The resort lends out kayaks and snorkel gear for free, so you can paddle out front and watch the fish, and after dark there's a beachside fire show the kids love. There's a playground and family rooms, prices start at about ฿2,500 a night, and the buffet breakfast is varied and fresh, eaten beachside in a lovely setting. Some suites have a private plunge pool or jacuzzi with a sea view. It's one of the 10 stays in this article that families pick most often. Honest notes from the reviews: there's no central pool; some rooms and bathrooms are starting to age, as the building has been open since 2006; hot water in some rooms is inconsistent and the air-con is loud in a few; restaurant service is fairly slow, especially at dinner; there are mosquitoes in the evening so bring your own repellent; the last stretch of the journey is up and down a slope; and Wi-Fi and signal on the island can be unstable. The bottom line: it's the best fit for families with young kids who want a private, shallow, clear-water beach on a reachable budget and don't mind rooms that are starting to age.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're travelling as a family, make the most of the resort's free kayaks and snorkel gear, and take the kids to the beachside fire show at night. If you want a bit more privacy, look at the Suite Pool Stone rooms with a private plunge pool.

entries.type: Beachfront Resort 3-Star · Beachfront on Lung Dam Beach
entries.name: Avatara Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Lung Dam Beach · 5–7 min walk to Sai Kaew/Ao Phai
entries.addr: 106 Moo 4, Lung Dam Beach, Phe Sub-district, Mueang Rayong
entries.storyHtml: Avatara Resort is the stay that honest takes from real reviews call a good fit for anyone who wants to sleep right by the sea on Koh Samet on a reachable budget — set in front of Lung Dam Beach, a resort of 59 rooms, scoring 8.6 from 464 reviews, with prices starting at just about ฿1,800 a night, one of the lightest entry points among the 10 stays in this article. The standout point guests mention is the Lung Dam Beach location, quieter than the main beaches — a few steps and you reach the sea and can go straight into the water — while it's also about a 5–7 min walk to Sai Kaew Beach and Ao Phai, so you get both quiet and convenience in one spot. The highlight reviews praise most is the buffet breakfast, with tables set on the sand looking out at the eastern sea, and a varied Thai and Western menu. After dark the beachside deck has a fire-twirling show that brings a fun atmosphere to dinner by the sea. Rooms are clean and larger than you'd expect for the price, and the staff are friendly in a family-resort way. Honest notes from the reviews: there's no pool here, so you swim in the sea instead; it's a resort that's been open since 2015, so some details are starting to age and room freshness isn't consistent across every room; the paths on the island are sand and dirt that aren't easy for dragging big suitcases; there's no lift; late-night service sometimes has no staff on duty; and prices over long weekends and high season climb fast, so book ahead. The bottom line: it suits anyone who wants to sleep by the sea, have breakfast on the sand, and watch a fire-twirling show on a budget, and who doesn't mind there being no pool.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Get up for the buffet breakfast on the sand on the east side in the morning light — that's when it looks its best. Book ahead over long weekends, since prices climb fast, and bring an easy-to-drag bag because the paths are sand.

entries.name: Samed Grandview Resort
entries.badge: 🚢 Near the pier, walk into the sea
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sai Kaew Beach · ~5 min walk from Na Dan pier
tags: 🚢 ~5 min walk from Na Dan pier
🏖️ On Sai Kaew Beach, straight into the sea
entries.addr: 8/1 Moo 4, Sai Kaew Beach, Phe Sub-district, Mueang Rayong
entries.storyHtml: Samed Grandview Resort is the option that honest takes from real reviews call the right fit for anyone who wants to stay on Sai Kaew Beach where you can walk into the sea in a few steps and be close to the pier — a 4-star resort of 77 rooms, scoring 8.5 from 239 reviews, sitting right on Sai Kaew Beach in the middle of the island's longest and liveliest stretch. The standout point guests like is the convenience: it's about a 5 min walk from the Na Dan pier, with no boat ride into a hidden beach like on the Ao Prao side, so you reach your stay almost as soon as you land — a big help if you're on a short trip or have a lot of luggage. Around it are the De Grand seaside restaurant, a pool, a spa, and restaurants and entertainment around the beach within walking distance. Some room categories are spacious and clean, the beds are comfortable, and breakfast earns praise for being varied and good value. Prices start at ฿2,500, more reachable than the luxury resorts on the west side. It's one of the 10 stays in this article that suits anyone who puts travel convenience first. Honest notes from the reviews: Sai Kaew Beach is lively and music from the bars around the beach carries late, so light sleepers should be prepared; room condition isn't consistent — some rooms are small, dimly lit, or have older furniture due for an update; you'll find the odd mosquito in the room, so bring your own repellent; and you should check the minibar bill and extra charges carefully at checkout. The bottom line: it suits anyone who wants to stay on Sai Kaew Beach, walk into the sea, be near the pier, and have restaurants around — and you should ask for an updated room far from the bars.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're on a short trip, this one wins on the 5 min walk from the Na Dan pier. Ask for an updated room facing the sea (Sea View), and check the minibar bill carefully at checkout.

entries.type: Beach Resort 3-Star · Beachfront on Ao Prao
entries.name: Lima Coco Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Prao · west side · reached by boat/vehicle across the island
tags: 🌊 Snorkel over coral off the beach
entries.addr: 40/1 Moo 4, Ao Prao Beach, Phe Sub-district, Mueang Rayong
entries.storyHtml: Lima Coco Resort is the option that honest takes from real reviews call the best value on Ao Prao for anyone who wants a private, clear-water beach on a light budget — a 3-star resort of 44 rooms, scoring 8.4 from 336 reviews, with prices starting at just about ฿1,500 a night, the lightest entry point among the 10 stays in this article. The main draw is the same as the luxury resorts on the same bay: Ao Prao, quiet with clear water, where you can snorkel over coral off the beach, and one of the best sunset-watching spots on Koh Samet. The highlight reviews like is the beachside pool that looks straight out at the sea, where you can sit and watch the sunset. Some villas climb the hillside with sea views and a balcony to sit out over Ao Prao. The food is tasty and reasonably priced, and the staff are friendly. The standout, in short, is getting the same beach and clear water as the luxury resorts on Ao Prao, but at a markedly lighter starting price. Honest notes from the reviews: some rooms and parts of the building are basic and look worn with age; some rooms are small, fairly dark, and short on storage; hot water is sometimes unstable and the temperature swings; the booking-site photos look newer than the real thing, so set your expectations right; getting there means a boat plus a vehicle across the island into the bay, so allow extra time; and the bay is so quiet there are almost no restaurants outside the resort and little to do. The bottom line: it suits anyone who wants the clear-water Ao Prao atmosphere on the lightest budget and is ready to accept a more basic room in exchange for the price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Set your expectations for room condition to match the price, and if you want a view go for Deluxe Sea View or Beachfront. Allow extra travel time for the boat and vehicle into Ao Prao, and head to the poolside to watch the sunset in the evening.

entries.name: Larissa Samed Resort
entries.revCount: Booking/Agoda 8.9 · 245 reviews · east side near Sai Kaew

tags: 🌿 Cottages in a leafy green garden
entries.addr: 8/1 Moo 4, Phe Sub-district, Mueang Rayong (east side near Sai Kaew Beach)
entries.storyHtml: Larissa Samed Resort is the stay that honest takes from real reviews call the best fit for anyone coming to Koh Samet for a quiet rest in a private seaside garden — a small cottage resort of just 24 rooms, scoring 8.9 from 245 reviews, set on the island's east side, away from the buzz of the main beaches but still about a 10 min walk to Sai Kaew Beach. What makes people like it is the feel of small cottages spread through a garden leafy with real trees and grass, plus a quiet private beach where you can snorkel over coral in the shallows. The thing reviews praise most is the cleanliness, which earns a high score of around 9.2, and the welcoming staff who look after you closely in a small-resort way. Rooms are clean and larger than many expect, comfortable to sleep in, and prices start at ฿2,050, good value against the average stay on Koh Samet. It rounds out the 10 stays in this article with an option that leans on cleanliness, quiet, and attentive service on a reachable budget. Honest notes from the reviews: there's no pool here and breakfast isn't included, so you'll need to plan where to eat in the morning; there are mosquitoes and insects natural to a garden resort; the private beach is more rocky than white sand; it's a small resort with limited availability that's hard to book at peak times; and some rooms show traces of age, as the building opened in 2009 and was refurbished in 2015. The bottom line: it suits couples and small families who want a quiet, clean corner in a private seaside garden, and who don't mind there being no pool and no included breakfast.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: A small resort of just 24 rooms fills up fast at peak times, so book ahead. Plan your own breakfast since it isn't included in the room rate, and bring mosquito repellent and shoes for walking on the rocks.

advice.head: Want a quiet, clear-water beach for snorkelling over coral
advice.bodyHtml: → Ao Prao Resort ฿3,500 or Lima Coco Resort ฿1,500 — both on Ao Prao, snorkel off the beach, lovely sunsets, on a lighter budget

advice.head: Want a lively location, walk to everything
advice.bodyHtml: → Sai Kaew Beach Resort ฿2,800 or Samed Grandview Resort ฿2,500 — on Sai Kaew Beach, walk to the sea, restaurants, and entertainment at night

advice.head: Travelling as a family with young kids
advice.bodyHtml: → Ao Cho Grandview Hideaway Resort ฿2,500, a private beach with shallow clear water, free kayaks and snorkels, fire show, playground

advice.head: Want to escape the bustle for the quiet island tip
advice.bodyHtml: → Mooban Talay Resort ฿2,500, at the island's tip on Ao Noina, garden bungalows, a near-private beach, sunset view

advice.head: Want a quiet, clean corner in a seaside garden
advice.bodyHtml: → Larissa Samed Resort ฿2,050, green-garden cottages with a private beach, high cleanliness score · or Samed Villa Resort ฿2,500, a leafy garden with a praised breakfast

advice.head: Want to sleep by the sea on the tightest budget
advice.bodyHtml: → Lima Coco Resort ฿1,500 or Avatara Resort ฿1,800 — both beachfront at the lightest starting prices in this article, with a buffet breakfast on the sand at Avatara

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates for standard rooms and may change by date and season; we recommend checking real prices and comparing 3 sites before every booking. The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms — we did not stay ourselves. Koh Samet sits within a national park, so there's a national park entry fee at the pier. There are no private cars on the island; you get around by shared songthaew or on foot. The Ao Prao beaches require a boat or a vehicle across the island into the bay, so allow extra travel time. Over long weekends and high season (November–April), prices rise and rooms sell out fast, so book 1–2 months ahead. It's a 3–3.5 hour trip from Bangkok to Ban Phe pier, then a boat across to the island. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about Koh Samet beach hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best beachfront hotel on Koh Samet?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style and the beach you like. By score and luxury, Le Vimarn Cottages & Spa has the highest score in this article at 9.3, a 5-star resort on Ao Prao. By number of reviews, Ao Cho Grandview Hideaway Resort has the most, over 2,990. For a lively location within walking distance of everything, Sai Kaew Beach Resort. For value with a high score, Samed Villa Resort (9.2) or Larissa Samed Resort (8.9)

faq.q: ❓ How much do Koh Samet beach hotels cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at about ฿1,500–4,500 per night. The lightest end is Lima Coco Resort from ฿1,500 and Avatara Resort from ฿1,800. The mid-range is Larissa (฿2,050), Samed Villa / Mooban Talay / Ao Cho / Samed Grandview (฿2,500), and Sai Kaew (฿2,800). The top end is Ao Prao (฿3,500) and Le Vimarn (฿4,500). Prices are approximate starting rates for standard rooms; over long weekends and high season they run higher than usual

faq.q: ❓ Which beach should you stay on at Koh Samet?
faq.a: Sai Kaew Beach suits anyone who likes a bit of buzz, within walking distance of restaurants and night entertainment (Sai Kaew Beach Resort, Samed Grandview Resort). Ao Prao on the west side suits anyone who wants a quiet, clear-water beach, coral snorkelling, and a sunset, but you have to take a boat into the bay (Le Vimarn, Ao Prao, Lima Coco). Ao Phai, Lung Dam Beach, Ao Cho, Ao Noina suit anyone who wants a quiet, private beach and families (Samed Villa, Avatara, Ao Cho, Mooban Talay)

faq.q: ❓ Is Koh Samet good for families with young kids, and where to stay?
faq.a: Very much so, especially beaches that are shallow and quiet. The best fit is Ao Cho Grandview Hideaway Resort, with a private beach of shallow clear water, free kayaks and snorkels, a fire show, and a playground. Next is Sai Kaew Beach Resort, with several pools and a kids' pool. And Samed Villa Resort, with a clear-water beach good for kids to play in the shallows

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Koh Samet, and do you have to take a boat?
faq.a: From Bangkok it's about a 3–3.5 hour drive to Ban Phe pier in Rayong, then a passenger ferry (~30–40 min) or speedboat (~15 min) across to the island, with a national park entry fee at the pier. Most stays on Sai Kaew Beach and the east side are walkable from the Na Dan pier, while the Ao Prao beaches on the west side require a further speedboat or vehicle across the island into the bay, so allow plenty of time

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book a Koh Samet hotel?
faq.a: Many beachfront resorts on Koh Samet are small stays (some with just 22–31 rooms), so they fill up fast. Over long weekends and high season (November–April), book 1–2 months ahead, especially Le Vimarn, Larissa, and Mooban Talay. Other times, 2–3 weeks is enough. Every platform offers Free Cancellation, so it's worth locking in a rate like that first if your plans aren't firm, then compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price
